# Personal Statement - Psychology (UK Application)

## Why do you want to study this course or subject?

My fascination with psychology began with simple questions: Why do we remember some things but forget others? How do children learn language so effortlessly? What makes each person unique?

What excites me most is how psychology combines scientific methods with understanding human experience. I'm particularly drawn to cognitive psychology because it explores how our minds work—from perception and memory to decision-making.

Reading about language development sparked my curiosity about how children acquire grammar rules without formal instruction. This led me to explore broader questions about learning that psychology seeks to answer.

I'm fascinated by how psychological research can improve lives through better educational methods, effective therapies, and mental health insights. The field's potential to bridge scientific understanding with practical applications makes it appealing.

## How have your qualifications and studies helped you to prepare for this course or subject?

My academic background has given me a strong foundation for psychology studies. Through reading psychology textbooks and research articles, I've developed skills in analyzing scientific studies and understanding how researchers test theories.

I've studied basic brain anatomy and learned about key areas like Broca's and Wernicke's areas, which are important for language processing. This helped me understand the biological basis of behavior and cognition.

My exploration of different psychological theories, particularly those about how we understand language and concepts, has taught me to think critically about competing explanations for human behavior. I've learned to evaluate evidence and consider how different research methods lead to different conclusions.

Studying linguistics has given me insights into how language works, which connects well with cognitive psychology's interest in mental processes. This background helps me appreciate how psychology investigates complex human abilities.

My interest in artificial intelligence has also been valuable, as it's helped me understand different approaches to studying the mind and appreciate what makes human cognition unique. I'm particularly fascinated by how we might apply psychological principles to improve how we communicate with AI systems—essentially using our understanding of human psychology to create better prompts and interactions with language models.

## What else have you done to prepare outside of education, and why are these experiences useful?

Outside formal studies, I've pursued activities that deepened my interest in psychology and prepared me for university-level study.

I started keeping a learning journal where I document psychological concepts and research findings, regularly updating my psychology learning notes website at https://zhangyulin-space.github.io/. This habit has helped me develop note-taking skills and connect ideas from different sources.

I developed ChatFerry, a philosophical dialogue game where players explore cognition, reality, and self through conversations with AI characters. This open-source project (https://github.com/zhangyulin-space/ChatFerry) combined psychology and technology to help teenagers with gaming addiction through meaningful philosophical discussion.

Creating ChatFerry taught me how psychological principles can be applied creatively to real problems. I incorporated therapeutic concepts like trust-building and emotional awareness into engaging mechanics. This showed psychology's potential to create meaningful interventions beyond traditional therapy.

I regularly watch psychology lectures online and read popular science books about mind and behavior. This keeps me engaged with current developments and helps develop critical thinking skills.

These activities have reinforced my enthusiasm for psychology and given me realistic expectations about studying human behavior scientifically.
